q: Under Building Maintenance, besides overseeing the physical condition of the building, what other duty does Sec. 2.1.1(c) assign to the Architect?
o: Personally supervise all tenant lease negotiations
Issue occupancy permits
Conduct annual structural audits under a separate SPP document
Monitor security services
n: Sec. 2.1.1(c) simply states the Architect shall "monitor security services." (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 2.1.1(c))

q: An architect is retained after turnover as Building Administrator and/or Property Manager of a commercial complex. Per Sec. 1.3, what is the underlying purpose of engaging the architect in this role?
o: To maximize the lifespan of the building/s in order to produce the maximum economic return
To satisfy a mandatory requirement that only architects may manage buildings
To reduce the architect's professional liability for design errors
To prepare the building for eventual demolition
n: Sec. 1.3 states the Architect may be engaged as Building Administrator and/or Property Manager "to maximize the lifespan of the building/s in order to produce the maximum economic return." (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 1.3)

q: Sec. 2.1.1(d) requires the Architect to monitor maintenance and upkeep services covering the cleanliness of which areas?
o: Only the main lobby and the building signage
Only the perimeter fence and guardhouse
Only the tenant units themselves
Corridors, lobbies, stairs, other common areas, exits, parking areas, and garbage collection
n: Sec. 2.1.1(d) covers "cleanliness of corridors, lobbies, stairs and other common areas, exits, parking areas, garbage collection." (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 2.1.1(d))

q: A building owner suspects the facility is no longer functioning as originally intended. Which Post-Construction Evaluation task under Sec. 2.2.1(a) directly addresses this concern?
o: Re-survey the property's lot boundaries
Evaluate the initial design program versus the actual use of the facility
Recompute the architect's original design fee
File a new building permit application
n: Sec. 2.2.1(a) requires the Architect to "evaluate the initial design program vs. the actual use of the facility." (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 2.2.1(a))

q: Under Building Equipment Maintenance (Sec. 2.1.3), the Architect assists proper third parties in seeing to it that which kinds of equipment are properly maintained and in good working condition?
o: Only office furniture and fixtures
Air-conditioning, sprinkler system, generators, transformers, and telecommunications equipment
Only elevators and escalators
Only the architect's own drafting equipment
n: Sec. 2.1.3(a) lists "air-conditioning, sprinkler system, generators, transformers, telecommunications equipment, etc." as equipment the Architect helps ensure is properly maintained. (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 2.1.3(a))

q: SPP Document 205 forms part of the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of which law?
o: Republic Act No. 545
Republic Act No. 9266 (Architecture Act of 2004)
Republic Act No. 8981
Presidential Decree No. 1096 (National Building Code)
n: The document's title block states it is "Part of the IRR of R.A. No. 9266," the Architecture Act of 2004. (Source: SPP Document 205, title block)

q: An architect who both designed and built a commercial complex is later asked to also handle its post-construction services in the same undertaking, without engaging a separate consultant. Under Sec. 3, which manner of providing services does this describe?
o: This arrangement is prohibited under SPP Document 205
Working in a dual capacity as Architect-of-record and Consulting Architect for post-construction services (Sec. 3.1)
Working solely as Consulting Architect for post-construction services only (Sec. 3.2)
This requires a separate license as a Property Manager
n: Sec. 3.1 describes exactly this dual-capacity arrangement, where the same architect who was Architect-of-record also serves as Consulting Architect for post-construction services. (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 3.1)

q: Sec. 2.2.1(d)'s reference to "forensic investigation" directs the reader to which other SPP document for further reference?
o: SPP Document 201
SPP Document 206
SPP Document 203
SPP Document 204
n: The text states "This is referred to as 'forensic investigation' of the building's systems (Reference Doc 203)." (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 2.2.1(d))

q: Under Grounds and Landscaping Supervision (Sec. 2.1.2), the Architect supervises landscape contractors and gardeners for what specific tasks?
o: Sourcing plant nursery suppliers only
Structural retrofitting of retaining walls
Installation of new landscape lighting fixtures
Proper watering, pruning, trimming and maintenance of both hardscapes and softscapes
n: Sec. 2.1.2(a) states the Architect shall "supervise landscape contractors and gardeners for the proper watering, pruning, trimming and maintenance of the landscape (both hardscapes and softscapes)." (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 2.1.2(a))

q: Sec. 2.2.1(b) requires the Architect, during Post-Construction Evaluation, to determine the effectiveness of which elements?
o: The tax assessment of the land only
The marketing strategy used to sell building units
The building's insurance coverage only
The various building systems and the materials systems in use
n: Sec. 2.2.1(b) states the Architect shall "determine the effectiveness of the various building systems and the materials systems in use." (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 2.2.1(b))

q: Water seepage and shrinkage cracks are discovered in a building years after turnover. Under Sec. 2.2.1(d), what is the Architect's role, and what is this activity called?
o: Ignore it, since post-construction defects fall outside SPP Document 205
Study, research, and give solutions to the discovered defects and failures — referred to as "forensic investigation" of the building's systems
Immediately demolish and rebuild the affected portion at the architect's own expense
Refer the matter exclusively to the local building official with no further architect involvement
n: Sec. 2.2.1(d) requires the Architect to study, research and give solutions to discovered/emerging/evolving defects and failures such as shrinkage and water seepage, and the document calls this a "forensic investigation" of the building's systems. (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 2.2.1(d))

q: An architect managing a commercial building wants to increase occupancy and properly bill tenants for shared costs. Per Sec. 2.1.4 (Business Development and Management), which pair of duties reflects this role?
o: Set the assessed value of the property for real property tax purposes
Negotiate the sale of the building on behalf of the owner
Draft the building's original architectural design and secure the building permit
Innovate schemes to attain maximum building occupancy, and bill tenants for rentals and utilities such as electricity, water, telephone, cable and gas
n: Sec. 2.1.4 assigns the Architect to innovate schemes for maximum occupancy (2.1.4a) and to bill tenants for rentals and utilities such as electricity, water, telephone, cable, gas and other related dues (2.1.4b). (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 2.1.4(a)-(b))

q: Under Sec. 1.1, building administration and management goes beyond mere maintenance and upkeep functions because it requires the services of what kind of professional?
o: A government building inspector
A licensed civil engineer specializing only in structural upkeep
A single-discipline maintenance contractor
A multi-disciplinary professional who can perform a wide range of functions for efficient and economical building operation
n: Sec. 1.1 states building administration and management requires "the services of a multi-disciplinary professional who can perform a wide range or functions for the efficient and economical operation and maintenance of a building, facility or a complex." (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 1.1)

q: Sec. 3 (Manner of Providing Services) provides that the Architect may enter into a contract with the Owner in two possible ways. What are they?
o: Working only during construction, or only after the defects liability period has lapsed
Working in a dual capacity as Architect-of-record and Consulting Architect for post-construction services, or working solely as Consulting Architect for post-construction services
Working only as a salaried employee of the Owner, or only as an unpaid volunteer consultant
Working exclusively through government appointment, or exclusively through private bidding
n: Sec. 3.1 and 3.2 give exactly these two manners of engagement. (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 3.1-3.2)

q: In addition to landscape supervision, Sec. 2.1.2(b) and (c) require the Architect to maintain which of the following?
o: Public roads outside the property boundary under LGU authority
Only the swimming pool and clubhouse facilities
Only the building's exterior paint finish
Orderly entrances, exits, and parking areas, plus streets i.e. road rights-of-way (RROWs), walkways, and ramps
n: Sec. 2.1.2(b) covers maintaining orderly entrances, exits and parking areas; Sec. 2.1.2(c) covers maintaining streets, i.e., road rights-of-way (RROWs), walkways, and ramps. (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 2.1.2(b)-(c))

q: Under Sec. 4 (Method of Compensation), how may the Architect be compensated for post-construction services?
o: A fixed one-time lump sum only, payable before construction begins
A percentage of gross rentals, maintenance and security fees, and/or a monthly salary/fee
Reimbursable expenses only, with no professional fee allowed
A percentage of the total construction cost only, per SPP Document 202
n: Sec. 4.1 allows a percentage of gross rentals, maintenance and security fees, and/or (Sec. 4.2) a monthly salary/fee. (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 4.1-4.2)

q: According to Sec. 1.2, the purpose of Post-Construction Services is to keep the channels of communication open among building owners, operators, architects, engineers, builders, and several other parties, in order to provide access to information regarding what?
o: The performance and upkeep of buildings
The zoning classification of the lot
The original design fees paid to the architect
The insurance premiums of the building owner
n: Sec. 1.2 says the open channels of communication exist "to provide access to information regarding the performance and upkeep of buildings." (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 1.2)

q: What is SPP Document 205, and what earlier document does it replace?
o: The Standard of Professional Practice on Construction Supervision, a wholly new document with no predecessor
The Standard of Professional Practice on Pre-Design Services, replacing UAP Doc. 201
The Code of Ethics for Architects, replacing the 1979 UAP Doc. 205
The Standard of Professional Practice on Post-Construction Services, replacing the 1979 UAP Doc. 205
n: SPP Document 205 is titled "Post-Construction Services" and expressly states it is replacing the 1979 UAP Doc. 205. (Source: SPP Document 205, title block)

q: As part of Building Maintenance duties, the Architect must formulate and enforce rules for the proper use of the building and facility. The source particularly emphasizes which areas?
o: Only the rooftop and basement levels
Only areas leased to third-party tenants
Common areas and the emergency/egress/exit areas
Only the owner's private office spaces
n: Sec. 2.1.1(b) directs the Architect to formulate and enforce rules for proper use of the building, "particularly in the common areas and the emergency/egress/exit areas." (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 2.1.1(b))

q: Post-Construction Evaluation under Sec. 2.2 is undertaken by the Architect under what triggering condition?
o: Only after a total building collapse
Upon the request of the Owner
Only when ordered by the Professional Regulation Board of Architecture
Automatically every calendar year regardless of the Owner's wishes
n: Sec. 2.2.1 begins: "Upon the request of the Owner, the Architect shall..." — evaluation is Owner-initiated, not automatic. (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 2.2.1)

q: Under Building Maintenance (Sec. 2.1.1), the Architect is tasked to see to it that the building and all its parts are in good condition. Which grouping of parts is named in the source?
o: Structure, plumbing, electrical, partitions, and finishes
Structure, landscaping, signage, and parking
Roofing, elevators, generators, and security cameras only
Foundation, fire exits, and elevators only
n: Sec. 2.1.1(a) requires the Architect to see that "the building and all the parts thereof (structure, plumbing, electrical, partitions, finishes, etc.) are all in good condition." (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 2.1.1(a))

q: Which of the following groups is explicitly named in Sec. 1.2 as part of the network kept in communication for Post-Construction Services?
o: Homeowners' association election committees
Foreign consular offices
Building research groups and utility providers
Land title registries and notaries public
n: Sec. 1.2 lists building owners, operators, architects, engineers, builders, manufacturers, building research groups, utility providers, furniture and equipment vendors, and building administrators/property managers. (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 1.2)

q: Sec. 1.3 lists the types of buildings, facilities, or complexes for which an Architect may serve as Building Administrator and/or Property Manager. Which set below matches the document?
o: Residential, industrial, heritage, or coastal
Commercial, industrial, residential, or institutional
Government, religious, industrial, or recreational
Commercial, agricultural, marine, or educational
n: Sec. 1.3 refers to "a commercial, industrial, residential or institutional building, facility or complex." (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 1.3)

q: Under Sec. 2.2.1(c), when evaluating the functional effectiveness of the design and construction process undertaken, the Architect's role is to do what?
o: Revoke the occupancy permit of the building
Personally reconstruct any defective portions of the building
Independently overturn the findings of the original structural engineer without consultation
Assist the proper third parties in evaluating the functional effectiveness of the design and construction process
n: Sec. 2.2.1(c) frames the Architect's role as assisting the proper third parties in this evaluation, not acting unilaterally. (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 2.2.1(c))
